name: Prednisone
summary: Oral prodrug corticosteroid converted to prednisolone; the workhorse systemic anti-inflammatory for allergic, autoimmune, and respiratory flares.
mechanism: Prodrug converted to prednisolone, a glucocorticoid receptor agonist that suppresses inflammation and immune responses at the transcriptional level.

pharmacokinetics.halfLife: Plasma ~2–3 h (prednisolone ~2–3.5 h); clinical effect persists longer
pharmacokinetics.onset: Oral: hours; clinical effect over 1–2 days
pharmacokinetics.duration: HPA suppression can outlast plasma levels with repeated dosing

dosing.adult: Indication-dependent; e.g., asthma/COPD exacerbation 40–60 mg daily for 5–7 days then taper; autoimmune flares often 0.5–1 mg/kg/day

safety.pregnancy: Crosses the placenta (partially inactivated by placental 11β-HSD2); use the lowest effective dose
safety.lactation: Low levels in breast milk; considered compatible at moderate doses — wait ~4 h after a dose
warnings: Adrenal suppression with prolonged use — taper to prevent adrenal crisis
Hyperglycemia, weight gain, mood changes, insomnia
Osteoporosis with long-term use — calcium/vitamin D and consider bisphosphonates
Avoid live vaccines during high-dose therapy
safety.overdose: Short-term overdose is rarely life-threatening; prolonged high dose causes cushingoid features and hyperglycemia — supportive care and gradual withdrawal

indications: Autoimmune disease flares (e.g., lupus, vasculitis, IBD)
clinicalPearls: Converted to prednisolone in the liver — consider prednisolone directly in severe hepatic impairment
Courses beyond 2–3 weeks require gradual taper to avoid adrenal insufficiency; take with food to reduce GI upset
good: Potent, inexpensive oral anti-inflammatory for moderate-to-severe flares
bad: Prolonged use without taper or bone protection; uncontrolled infection; live vaccines at high doses

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
